cells.tense: You are here with the pen, naming what a thing meant while it is still here.
cells.ask: Say that feeling out loud to one person, then sit ten seconds without adding anything to it.
cells.core:
Something landed today and it could be said plainly: this is what it meant. Saying it without decorating it, and then listening while the other person says their own piece back, is the whole thing. Nothing gets swallowed to keep the peace and nothing gets pushed onto anyone else. The exchange finishes clean because both people were in it in their own shape — one at each end, neither taken over by the other.

Most moments don't get their feeling gathered like that. Speaking what you feel and staying separate while you do it is one motion, not two, and it's the motion this seat is for. So give one exchange today a little more than it asks for: speak the feeling, leave room for theirs, and keep the wholeness rather than handing it away.
cells.sheetLine: You can say the whole of a feeling and stay whole in it.
cells.verb: arriving at the whole of what you feel, right to the edge where it's finished and wants to move
cells.place: the doorway of a finished thing, where the last piece of it gets gathered up and let go

cells.tense: You are standing at a future ending and writing its report before it can arrive.
cells.ask: Write one sentence naming what you fear will be lost when this ends, then let the day pass with no further action.
cells.core:
The whole feeling is there, and so is the ending ahead of it — so the goodbye is getting done early. The door gets checked for cracks before the thing itself arrives, and the version where it holds gets imagined, and what went wrong gets drawn up so it can't surprise anyone. Nothing completes at that speed.

What gets lost is the recognition that honors both sides — the exchange gets summarised into a report, and a report is not what friendship or a good day is for. Pick the one thing you actually want and let the day answer it. That is direction held in the present, instead of a verdict handed down before the moment has had its say.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door whose closed side you have stopped looking at.
cells.ask: Say one feeling out loud, badly, to one safe person this week — nothing more than that.
cells.core:
Something ended and the feeling of it went quiet without any decision being made about that. Since then it is hard to tell your own feeling from what you are supposed to be feeling, so you stay a step off — near the doorway of a thing rather than inside it, and not much lands. The whole gathered feeling is not in reach right now.

The beginning of it still is — the spark that does not know where it is going yet, and does not need to. Fresh things can reach it. Let somewhere new be new: one feeling said in the open, no shaping, no plan for how it should come out. The point is not to finish the feeling. The point is to let one arrive.

cells.tense: The pen is down while you decide, every day, what counted and what is over.
cells.ask: Name one thing you know is yours to finish, and say it out loud to yourself as yours.
cells.core:
There is a quiet sense of what is fair and when something is finished — it turns up when a tab gets picked up right, when someone got thanked properly, when a moment was too good to leave early. Following it without calling it anything makes it look like just being sensible: all sides even, the record clean, nobody having to say the awkward thing.

But every fair end nearby is being held up by that judgment, and by the whole feeling for what is complete. That is the part no one has said out loud — that you are the one drawing that line, and the line is yours.
